entry.title: Spray Fires: Fire Hazards from Aerosol Cans

media:group.media:title: Spray Fires: Fire Hazards from Aerosol Cans
media:group.media:description:
Experimental testing was conducted to explore the fire hazards associated with pressurized spray commodities. Advanced measurement tools captured detailed data on fireball size, pressure, heat flux, and other key measurements. The results provide critical insights into the potential for explosive fireballs in accident scenarios involving combustible spray contents. This data supports the development and justification of safety regulations for the transport of hazardous spray commodities under severe accident conditions.
This work was done in collaboration with the U.S. Department of Transportation’s Pipeline and Hazardous Materials Safety Administration (US-DOT-PHMSA).
SAND2026-22491V

entry.title: Object recognition at the speed of light: Sandia’s neuromorphic breakthrough

media:group.media:title: Object recognition at the speed of light: Sandia’s neuromorphic breakthrough
media:group.media:description:
Sandia researchers are reimagining object recognition by teaching optical materials to recognize quickly patterns. This neuromorphic approach allows light to pass through a trained material layer that instantly classifies what it sees. This breakthrough capability could greatly benefit many types of systems that use sensors to capture information.
For more information visit: https://www.sandia.gov/research/quickcuts

media:group.media:title: MANTIS: Sandia’s Horizontal Simulated Wellbore Testbed
media:group.media:description:
The Measurement and Assessment for Novel Technologies in Instrumentation and Sensing (MANTIS) testbed is a 1000-foot horizontal facility designed to replicate typical well conditions to assess tools and sensors for geothermal applications, oil and gas and carbon sequestration.
Learn more about Sandia’s geothermal research at https://energy.sandia.gov/programs/renewable-energy/geothermal-research/.
SAND2026-26692V

entry.title: Sandia's Ducted Fuel Injection Research Aims to Lower Costs and Emissions from Heavy-Duty Engines

media:group.media:title: Sandia's Ducted Fuel Injection Research Aims to Lower Costs and Emissions from Heavy-Duty Engines
media:group.media:description:
Ducted Fuel Injection (DFI) is a simple, retrofittable, in-cylinder technology for improving combustion in engines, reducing the amounts of fuel consumed and pollutants produced in doing the same amount of work. By using existing supply chains, infrastructure, and equipment, DFI provides a valuable opportunity to improve the economics and reduce the environmental footprint of applications that are unlikely to quickly electrify or switch to carbon-free fuels due to higher costs.
SAND2026 26370V

entry.title: R&D 100 Winner 2026: Grayscale Lithography through Annealed Resin Engineering (GLARE)

media:group.media:title: R&D 100 Winner 2026: Grayscale Lithography through Annealed Resin Engineering (GLARE)
media:group.media:description:
GLARE is a novel technique for creating grayscale photolithography masks quickly and affordably by turning 3D polymer patterns into carbon. This approach drastically reduces mask production time and cost, enabling faster, cheaper development of complex microstructures for applications like AR/VR lenses, spectroscopy, and advanced optics, opening new opportunities for startups and established industries alike.
SAND2026-20739V

media:group.media:title: R&D 100 Winner 2026: LAPIS
media:group.media:description:
Researchers at Sandia have developed LAPIS, a compiler that automatically transforms high-level programs into efficient, portable C++ code optimized for CPUs and GPUs in supercomputers. LAPIS makes it easier to implement algorithms for simulations and data analytics, and enables simpler integration of machine learning models into existing high-performance applications.
SAND2026-21245V

media:group.media:title: R&D 100 Winner 2026: Fenix
media:group.media:description:
Fenix is a breakthrough software framework that makes supercomputers more efficient and reliable by quickly recovering from hardware failures with minimal impact on performance, using a new pseudo-local recovery method that requires little change to existing applications. This technology can significantly reduce wasted computing time, lower energy consumption, and help large-scale computing centers meet growing demands—making high-performance computing faster and more cost-effective.
SAND2026-21621V

entry.title: Sandia’s Mobile Gun Test Complex: The Davis Gun

media:group.media:title: Sandia’s Mobile Gun Test Complex: The Davis Gun
media:group.media:description:
Watch Sandia Labs’ mobile Davis gun fire a BLU-109 earth penetrator into a specially selected geological target. The earth penetrator, or “bullet,” is shot from the Davis gun at speeds faster than the speed of sound, or Mach 1. A 4,000-pound steel reaction mass exits from the top of the barrel, soaring one mile high before it falls about 1,000 feet downrange.
Sandia’s Davis gun allows researchers to bring tests directly to the target, whether natural geology or engineered structures, with precise control over impact angle, speed, location and timing. This capability offers a significant advantage over other testing methods, like aircraft drops.
Sandia's Mobile Gun Test Complex includes three guns with interchangeable barrels in 16-inch, 12-inch and 8-inch sizes, providing flexibility for different experiments.
Subscribe to learn more about Sandia’s cutting-edge research and testing technologies.
SAND2021-9847V
